title: U.S. House · Florida's 28th District
area: Southern Miami-Dade and the Florida Keys (Monroe County), including Homestead, Florida City and Key West.

context.text: Both major-party primaries were canceled: incumbent Carlos Gimenez advanced unopposed as the Republican nominee, and Phil Ehr advanced unopposed as the Democratic nominee. Eddy Rojas is running with No Party Affiliation.

candidates.name: Carlos Gimenez
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Republican primary, unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Florida's 28th District (since 2023); in Congress since 2021

summary.text: Carlos Gimenez is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 28th District, first elected to the U.S. House in 2020. He spent 25 years in the City of Miami Fire Department, serving as its chief for the last nine, then served as Miami city manager, Miami-Dade County commissioner and Mayor of Miami-Dade County (2011-2020). His House committee work includes Armed Services and Homeland Security.

background.text: Born in 1954 in Cuba; according to his official House biography, he arrived in the United States shortly after the Communist takeover of Cuba and settled in Miami's Little Havana neighborhood.

Graduated from Christopher Columbus High School in Westchester, Florida, and earned a bachelor's degree in public administration from Barry University (1999, per Ballotpedia); he also completed the Program for Senior Executives in State and Local Government at Harvard's John F. Kennedy School of Government.

Joined the City of Miami Fire Department in 1975 and spent 25 years as a firefighter, the last nine as the department's chief; his House biography describes him as the first Cuban American to serve as Miami's fire chief.
Appointed Manager of the City of Miami in 2000, overseeing a budget of about $500 million and nearly 4,000 employees.
Elected Miami-Dade County Commissioner for District 7 in 2004 and served until 2011.
Elected Mayor of Miami-Dade County in 2011, re-elected in 2012 and 2016, and served until 2020.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2020. His official biography describes him as the first career firefighter-paramedic to serve in Congress.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the Homeland Security Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Transportation and Maritime Security; also a member of the House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party and the Smithsonian Board of Regents, and Vice Chairman of the Republican Governance Group.
According to his House biography, he is married to Lourdes and they have three adult children and six grandchildren.

priorities.text: Economy and Taxes: says lowering taxes, reforming the legal system to reduce undue liability for businesses, cutting regulations, and fostering a strong business climate are needed to sustain small-business growth.
Energy: supports an "all-of-the-above" approach to domestic energy production, opposes offshore drilling off Florida's coast, and supports deployment of clean-energy technology.

Immigration: prioritizes border-security resources alongside a path to legal status for undocumented immigrants already in the country, and continuation of DACA and Deferred Enforced Departure for Venezuelans.

positions.summary: On his official issues page, supports devoting more resources to border security and opposes sanctuary cities that limit local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, but also supports a path to legal status (rather than deportation) for undocumented immigrants already in the country, continuation of DACA, and Deferred Enforced Departure for Venezuelans.
Opposes raising the corporate tax rate above 21% or creating a new annual wealth tax, and opposes raising tax rates on corporations and small businesses to pay for new spending.
positions.quote: I also oppose increasing tax rates on corporations and small businesses as a means of paying for new spending and oppose the implementation of an annual wealth tax.

positions.summary: Says he supports an "all-of-the-above" approach to domestic energy that includes research and deployment of clean-energy technology and opposes offshore drilling off Florida, while also saying America must maintain energy independence through an all-of-the-above approach.
positions.quote: I support an all-of-the-above approach to domestic energy production with a focus on research, and deployment of new, clean energy technologies that ensures all Americans have access to affordable and reliable energy sources.

positions.summary: In November 2024 applauded President-elect Trump's plan for a 25% tariff on all products imported from Mexico and Canada until the drug and border crisis is resolved.
positions.quote: I applaud President Donald Trump's decision to implement a 25% tariff on all products coming into the United States until the drug and border crisis is resolved.

record.text: Serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, the Committee on Homeland Security (chairing the Subcommittee on Transportation and Maritime Security), and the House Armed Services Committee in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Phil Ehr
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Democratic primary, unopposed.

summary.text: Phil Ehr is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 28th Congressional District. He is a retired U.S. Navy officer who has run for Congress in prior cycles.

background.text: Born in Colorado and lived for many years in Pensacola before moving to West Kendall in Miami-Dade County, according to the Florida Keys Citizen.

Attended King's College London, earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of the State of New York and a master's degree in international relations from Troy State University.

Served in the U.S. Navy from 1982 to 2008 and retired as a commander; the Florida Keys Citizen reports his early assignments included the Mariel boatlift and work at Naval Air Station Key West with the Joint Interagency Task Force South.
Ran for Florida's 1st Congressional District in 2018 as a Democrat and lost the August primary to Jennifer Zimmerman, 60.5% to 39.5%.
Won the Democratic nomination in Florida's 1st District in 2020 after the primary was canceled, and lost the general election to Rep. Matt Gaetz, 64.6% to 34.0%.
Entered the 2024 U.S. Senate Democratic primary in Florida in July 2023, then withdrew in October 2023 to challenge Rep. Carlos Gimenez in the 28th District.
Lost the 2024 general election to Gimenez, 64.6% to 35.4%, and is again the Democratic nominee in 2026 after the August 18 primary was canceled.

priorities.text: Reducing Florida's cost of living and strengthening Medicare and Social Security.
Securing the border and reforming legal immigration.
Supporting public education and labor unions in Florida, and protecting the environment through clean energy and water infrastructure.

positions.summary: His 2024 campaign website (quoted on Ballotpedia) lists enacting responsible gun laws among his priorities.
positions.quote: Stop the mass murder epidemic by enacting responsible gun laws

candidates.researchNotes: Ehr has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His current 2026 campaign website's issues page could not be loaded (server error), so his priorities and positions are drawn from a campaign-website quote from his 2024 run for this same seat, the most recent statement of his positions found on Ballotpedia.

statements.quote: Secure our borders & reform legal immigration

candidates.name: Eddy Rojas

summary.text: Eddy Rojas is a No Party Affiliation candidate for Florida's 28th District. According to his campaign website, he came to Miami from Cuba and spent about 20 years building a service company. He ran for Mayor of Miami-Dade County in 2024.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he came to Miami from Cuba and over the past 20 years built a service company from the ground up, starting by parking cars.
Ran in the nonpartisan August 20, 2024 primary for Mayor of Miami-Dade County, receiving 1.3% (3,609 votes); Daniella Levine Cava won the primary with 57.9%.
Describes his campaign values as family, faith and hard work.

priorities.text: Cut regulations, lower taxes on small businesses and bring jobs to Miami.
priorities.quote: I'll fight to cut burdensome regulations, lower taxes on small businesses, and bring good-paying jobs back to Miami.

priorities.text: Education: school choice, vocational training and affordable higher education.
Safe communities: supporting law enforcement, securing borders and funding crime-prevention programs.

positions.summary: Says he will fight for school choice.
positions.quote: I will fight for school choice, vocational training, and affordable higher education

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from his campaign website priorities page; no Ballotpedia survey completed, and the site gives no further detail on policy.

statements.quote: I will support our law enforcement, secure our borders, and invest in community programs that prevent crime
statements.context: On his campaign website's priorities page
